ns2:section.sectionText: Using the case study method and discussion problems, graduate students in this course will study how laws in the U.S. regulate the use of natural resources, including public ownership and preservation of natural resources through other federal and state public lands. Also examines major federal environmental statues designed to protect natural resources, including the Clean Water Act, the Endangered Species Act, the National Environmental Policy Act, and federal acts related to forest, national parks, and wilderness protection. Students will asynchronously watch recordings of NRES 425 class meetings and participate in an additional graduate student only discussion session on Monday evenings. Required Text: Kein, Cheever, and Birdsong, Natural Resources Law: Placed Based Book of Cases and Problems 3rd edition published by Wolters Kluwer (ISBN: 978-1-4548-2509-8) Online scheduled class sessions require each student to have high speed internet access and either a headset with microphone or an external microphone and speakers so they may participate in the class discussions. Wireless internet is not recommended. Center for Innovation in Teaching & Learning (CITL) restrictions and assessments apply, see http://www.citl.illinois.edu.
